title: Grateful Dead Live at Lusk Field House, S.U.C.N.Y on 1971-04-18

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1971 Cortland show captured on a crisp soundboard tape; standout performances of Hard To Handle, Good Lovin', China Cat Sunflower / I Know You Rider and others.
ai_review.review: The concert delivers a raw, intense first set that builds into an even tighter second set, highlighted by a scorching Hard To Handle, a monster Good Lovin' jam, and a funky China Cat > I Know You Rider. The soundboard source is generally clear with only minor tape‑hiss, though the organ sits low in the mix. Overall the band sounds tight, the crowd vibe is electric, and Pigpen’s banter adds extra flavor.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (≈80%) are 4‑5 stars praising the performance and noting good soundboard quality; only a few early mixed comments lower the average slightly, leading to an overall strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with prominent guitars and bass; slight tape hiss noted but not distracting. Organ is very low/inaudible in places, but overall the recording captures the band well.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: A powerful opening set (CR&S, MABM) flows into a high‑octane second set with strong jams and Pigpen’s lively banter; the pacing stays tight throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar is described as loud, prominent and tightly in the pocket; reviewers note the band sounded "tight" and "funky."
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil's bass is highlighted as powerful and dominant – described as "demonic" and "very prominent" throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen gets major praise for his rap on Good Lovin', his humorous banter before Next Time You See Me, and overall hot, energetic presence.
band_member_comments.Keys: The organ is noted as virtually inaudible or very low in the mix; no dedicated keyboardist present in this era.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is called steady and solid, with a notable drum solo during Good Lovin' that reviewers enjoyed.
